title: Min Stack: O(1) push/pop/top/getMin.
shortTitle: Min Stack: O(1) push, pop, top, and getMin
keyPoints: Maintain a second stack whose top always holds the minimum so far, updated on every push and pop.
On push: push to main and push min(value, currentMin) to the auxiliary stack.
On pop: pop both stacks in lockstep so the minimum stays correct.
getMin is O(1): just peek the auxiliary stack.
Space-optimized variant pushes to min stack only on <=; the <= vs < distinction matters for duplicates.
Delta-encoding variant encodes minimum changes in a single stack but sacrifices readability.

s1_definition.oneliner: Keep a second stack whose top always holds the minimum so far, pushing and popping it in lockstep with the main stack.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **Min Stack** – a stack supporting push, pop, top, and getMin, all in O(1) time.
- **Auxiliary stack** – mirrors the main stack; each entry records the minimum of all elements from the bottom to that level.
- **Push** – push value to main; push `min(value, mins.peek())` to auxiliary.
- **Pop** – pop both stacks together.
- **getMin** – peek the auxiliary stack.
- **Space** – O(n) extra; optimized variant pushes only new minimums with `<=`.
s1_definition.analogy: At the National Bank of India, the manager stacks deposit slips and must instantly answer "what is the smallest deposit still in this pile?" A clerk keeps a shadow pile where each slip records the smallest amount seen up to that point. When a slip is removed from the real pile, the matching shadow slip is removed too, so the top of the shadow pile is always the current smallest.

sections.s3_flow:
```text
  Two-Stack Min Stack
  ───────────────────
  Push: 5, 1, 7

  Main Stack     Min Stack
  ┌─────┐        ┌─────┐
  │  7  │ top    │  1  │ top ← getMin()
  ├─────┤        ├─────┤
  │  1  │        │  1  │
  ├─────┤        ├─────┤
  │  5  │        │  5  │
  └─────┘        └─────┘

  pop(7): both stacks pop
  Main: [1,5]  Min: [1,5] → getMin()=1

  pop(1): both stacks pop
  Main: [5]  Min: [5] → getMin()=5
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
A Min Stack supports push, pop, top, and getMin all in O(1) by keeping a second auxiliary stack whose top always holds the current minimum. On every push, I push the value to main and the smaller of the value and the current minimum to the auxiliary. On every pop, I pop both in lockstep. The getMin operation is a single peek.

The invariant is that at every level the auxiliary entry is the smallest value present from the bottom to that level. Popping in lockstep maintains this automatically. For banking money I use `BigDecimal` with `compareTo` to ensure correct scale and precision.

The space-optimized variant pushes to the min stack only when the value is `<=` the current minimum, and pops only when the removed value equals the minimum. The `<=` vs `<` distinction is critical: strict `<` fails to track duplicate minimums. A third approach encodes deltas in a single stack but trades clarity for O(1) extra space.

In my project at the National Bank of India, the trading desk stages pending orders on a stack and the risk monitor queries the smallest pending amount at every instant. The min stack answers in O(1) regardless of how rapidly orders churn.

Remember one sentence: keep a parallel min stack in lockstep so getMin is always a single peek in O(1).
